replies.content: Easier to see that you've installed it correctly between the ptfe washers.

content:
In a later stage an aligner is used on these spacers while the screw are placed. I don't know if I got a bunk aligner tool, but there is simply no way to get it on the spacers without exerting some force, which pushes them off the track, since the grooves are pointed outwards.

I aligned them exactly backwards from what is instructed here in order to be able to use the aligner tool. Then, after I got a screw lightly in each one, I went back around, reorienting them to point outwards, and used the aligner tool again.
all the spacers have varying degrees of movement with the screws fully tightened. Some could move in a strong breeze. Others, you have to nudge slightly. Hopefully that doesn't matter
Make sure you only put the screws in until they bottom, do not tighten them. You will tear a washer. I backed mine off 1/8 a turn and then snugged them down.

I didn't have an issue adding the spacers as directed... that is, after tightening the screws in the previous step. You do have to be very careful to align them properly and push them in very carefully.  I just had a thumb and pointer finger on each side and carefully pushed or pulled them into place while wiggling them back and forth a little.  However, I do see it being easier and less likely to break something if you left the screws loose and then inserted the spacers before tightening the screws.

The new expansion joints located in the corners are now oriented 90 degrees differently than the previous ones. I am really curious for the technical reasoning behind this. The old orientation made more sense from a thermal expansion/joint flexion point of view.
I tightened the screws and then realized I couldn’t slide the joints in so I just loosened the screws and tightened them again when I had them on.

replies.content: Same here, I damaged one of the washers before I realized I need to loosen the screws

content: Dont tighten hem.do it after inserting the joints. I broke a washer because the joint tore it when inserting.

replies.content:
I second this approach, to prevent damaging the nylon washers. Combined mounting screws + washers + expansion joint per set at the time, and then tightened the set. And repeated that.

Also used Tjackal's tip to use the pulley spacer "X and Y" tool between the washers, when inserting the expansion joint.

Thanks!

I damaged a washer trying to insert the joint.
So I did like 3Dmountains.

content: I'm assuming a little bit of resistance when wedging the expansion joint between the washers is expected.
If you have fat fingers like me, use the pulley spacer tool (the one with X and Y markings) to separate the two washers and keep them separate while inserting the joint!
Once sliding the expansion joint on, should the screw be tightened in order to hold the expansion joint in place?

replies.content: No, the screw cannot be tightened any further at this point. The expansion joint will be secured later when the heatbed is installed.
